title: Keypad Safe
intro: Type the secret code on a keypad to unlock a safe. A servo opens the lock.

wiring_steps.title: The keypad
wiring_steps.text: Unplug the USB cable before you change any wires. Plug it back in when you're done. Start with the power rails: a black wire from GND on your board to the blue (−) rail at the bottom of the breadboard, and a red wire from {{VCC}} to the red (+) rail. The keypad has eight pins on its ribbon. From left to right they are rows R1 to R4, then columns C1 to C4. Wire each one to the pin with the same name: R1 to {{pin:KEYPAD_R1}}, R2 to {{pin:KEYPAD_R2}}, R3 to {{pin:KEYPAD_R3}}, R4 to {{pin:KEYPAD_R4}}, C1 to {{pin:KEYPAD_C1}}, C2 to {{pin:KEYPAD_C2}}, C3 to {{pin:KEYPAD_C3}} and C4 to {{pin:KEYPAD_C4}}. Take your time and check each one!

wiring_steps.title: The LCD screen
wiring_steps.text: Connect the four pins on the back of the LCD (the I2C backpack) with wires: GND to the blue (−) rail, VCC to the red (+) rail, SDA to {{pin:SDA}} and SCL to {{pin:SCL}}.

wiring_steps.title: The servo lock
wiring_steps.text: Plug three wires into the servo's plug: brown (or black) to the blue (−) rail, red to the red (+) rail, and orange (or yellow) to {{pin:SERVO_PIN}}.

steps.title: Read the keypad
steps.text:
A 4 × 4 keypad has 16 buttons in rows and columns. The **Keypad** library works out which key is pressed. `getKey()` gives the key, or nothing if no key is pressed.

**Your task:** Run, open the **Serial Monitor**, and press some keys.
hints: Each key appears once per press.
In the simulator, click the keypad's keys.
If the wrong keys appear, the row and column wires might be swapped.

checks.label: The keys I press show up

steps.success: 16 buttons, and only 8 wires! The rows-and-columns trick saves pins.

steps.title: Hello, LCD
steps.text:
The LCD shows 2 rows of 16 letters. `setCursor(column, row)` chooses where the next letters go (counting from 0).

**Your task:** change the second row to your own message, then Run.
hints: Change the text inside the second `lcd.print`.
Keep it to 16 letters or fewer.
If the screen is blank, turn the little blue knob on the back to change the contrast.

steps.title: Type the code
steps.text:
Collect the keys in a **String** called `entered`. When `#` is pressed, compare it with the secret code. The screen shows `*` for each key, so nobody can see the code over your shoulder.

**Your task:** fill in the blanks.
hints: Compare what was typed with the secret code.
`+=` adds the new key onto the end of the String.
steps.success: Your code checker works, and it keeps the code hidden.

steps.title: The safe
steps.text: **Goal:** a real safe. The right code then `#` opens the lock (servo to 90°) and shows `OPEN`. `*` locks it again (servo to 0°). After 3 wrong codes, make guessers wait 10 seconds.
hints: Add the Servo library and `lock.attach(SERVO_PIN);` in `setup()`.
Count wrong tries in a variable; reset it when the code is right.

checks.label: The right code opens the lock

steps.success: A working safe! Limiting wrong tries is how phones stop people guessing PINs.

outro: Your safe checks a secret code, hides it as you type, and locks out guessers. You used **Strings**, a **keypad library**, an **LCD**, and thought about **security**.
stretch: Let the owner change the code: type the old code, then # then a new one.
After 3 wrong codes, lock the keypad for 30 seconds with a countdown.
Add a buzzer: a happy sound for the right code, a buzz for the wrong one.
